sources.institution: International Journal of Advanced Computer Science and Applications / The Science and Information Organization
sources.title: Mechatronics Design and Development of T-EVA: Bio-Sensorized Space System for Astronaut’s Upper Body Temperature Monitoring During Extravehicular Activities on the Moon and Mars
sources.suggested_citation: Palacios, P., Cornejo, J., Chavez, J. C., Cornejo, C., Cornejo, J., Vargas, M., Vargas-Cuentas, N. I., Roman-Gonzalez, A., & Valdivia-Silva, J. (2023). Mechatronics Design and Development of T-EVA: Bio-Sensorized Space System for Astronaut’s Upper Body Temperature Monitoring During Extravehicular Activities on the Moon and Mars. International Journal of Advanced Computer Science and Applications, 14(9), 661–672. https://doi.org/10.14569/IJACSA.2023.0140969
sources.source_scope: Supports an engineering description of an upper-body temperature-sensing garment, sensor placements, electronics, and prototype testing reported by the authors.
sources.evidence_limitations: This is a prototype/design report, not flight qualification, clinical validation, a core-temperature measurement validation, or a diagnostic/alert threshold source. The article describes further MDRS and lunar-like environment testing as future work. Its text appears internally inconsistent when it describes the DS18B20 as an analog 10 mV/°C device; do not reuse that hardware specification without checking the manufacturer datasheet and exact probe assembly.
sources.metadata_note: The supplied short Google share URL was not independently resolvable in the research browser. The canonical publisher record was matched by exact title and DOI; cite the DOI rather than the share URL. IJACSA describes submissions as double-blind peer reviewed; the individual article’s review history is not public.

sources.institution: International Astronautical Federation (IAF); bibliographic metadata also indexed by UTEC CRIS
sources.title: Biomedical Embedded System for Monitoring Temperature in Spacesuits During Extravehicular Activities in Analog Missions for Mars and the Moon
sources.suggested_citation: Palacios, P., et al. (2024). Biomedical Embedded System for Monitoring Temperature in Spacesuits During Extravehicular Activities in Analog Missions for Mars and the Moon. In 27th IAA Symposium on Human Exploration of the Solar System (pp. 468–478). International Astronautical Federation. https://doi.org/10.52202/078359-0051
sources.source_scope: The institutional abstract describes an in-suit temperature-sensor network connected to an embedded board, wrist display, and mission control, with simulated lunar/Martian testing proposed as future work.
sources.evidence_limitations: The public record is an abstract/metadata source. It describes a prototype and future analog-environment work; it does not establish flight or clinical validation and provides no ASTHRAL-ready medical threshold. Full text is sold by the proceedings distributor; ASTHRAL does not redistribute it.
sources.metadata_note: Author-list metadata conflict: the UTEC institutional record and proceedings.com item page list different co-author names/order. The short citation uses “et al.”; verify against the original proceedings title page before publishing a full author list.

sources.institution: IEEE; bibliographic metadata from UTEC CRIS
sources.title: Space Agriculture and Mechatronic Technologies: Micro-Review and Multi-Collaborative Study
sources.suggested_citation: Barreto, R., Cornejo, J., Palomares, R., Cornejo, J. A., Suárez-Quispe, J. C., Vargas, M., Valenzuela, C., Chavez, J. C., & Valdivia, J. (2023). Space Agriculture and Mechatronic Technologies: Micro-Review and Multi-Collaborative Study. In 2023 2nd International Conference for Innovation in Technology (INOCON 2023), Bangalore, India (pp. 1–8). https://doi.org/10.1109/INOCON57975.2023.10101312
sources.source_scope: A micro-review/conference contribution about controlled-environment space agriculture, mechatronics, and prospective food-production systems for long-duration missions.
sources.evidence_limitations: Relevant to agriculture and mechatronics context only. It is not evidence for EVA temperature sensing, astronaut physiology, thermal safety limits, medical alerts, or clinical interpretation. Full text remains subject to IEEE copyright; only metadata and a project-authored summary are included.

sources.institution: NASA Office of the Chief Health and Medical Officer
sources.title: OCHMO-TB-050: NASA-STD-3001 Technical Brief — Spacesuits (Volume 2, Revision E basis)
sources.publication_date: 2025-09-08 (brief date; derived from NASA-STD-3001 Volume 2 Revision E)
sources.suggested_citation: NASA Office of the Chief Health and Medical Officer. (2025). OCHMO-TB-050: Spacesuits (NASA-STD-3001 Technical Brief; based on Volume 2, Revision E). https://www.nasa.gov/wp-content/uploads/2025/09/ochmo-tb-050-spacesuits.pdf
sources.source_scope: Provides NASA program-design context on suited operations, heat storage, physiological monitoring, and the derivation of some spacesuit requirements.
sources.evidence_limitations: The document says it is for reference and does not supersede or waive agency, program, or contract requirements. It is based on Volume 2 Revision E, not the current Volume 2 Revision F. Do not transplant its numerical requirements or supporting thresholds into ASTHRAL without controlled program applicability and independent review.

sources.institution: NASA Johnson Space Center / NASA Technical Reports Server
sources.title: Core Body Temperature Predictions Using Metabolic Energy Expenditure and Heart Rate During Simulated Extravehicular Activity
sources.suggested_citation: Hoffmann, B., Cooper, L., York, S., Heinemann, K., Schlotman, T., Marshall-Goebel, K., & Buckland, D. (2024). Core Body Temperature Predictions Using Metabolic Energy Expenditure and Heart Rate During Simulated Extravehicular Activity. 53rd International Conference on Environmental Systems (ICES 2024). NASA Technical Reports Server. https://ntrs.nasa.gov/citations/20230016649
sources.source_scope: Describes a core-temperature prediction model using heart rate and metabolic rate in simulated EVA; the study collected local skin and suit cooling-garment temperatures and tested in a separate suited simulator dataset.
sources.evidence_limitations: Small simulator datasets (development n=6; test n=6), not in-flight or clinical validation. The reported prediction error is study-specific; it is not a diagnostic threshold, a sensor accuracy claim, or evidence that a model transfers to other suits, missions, populations, or gravity contexts.

sources.institution: NASA Open Science Data Repository / RadLab
sources.title: RadLab Data API
sources.suggested_citation: NASA Open Science Data Repository. (Dynamic; reviewed 2026-11-15). RadLab Data API. https://visualization.osdr.nasa.gov/radlab/gui/data-api/
sources.source_scope: Documents the public GET API, supported query forms, returned fields and source units: absorbed dose rate μGy/hour, dose equivalent rate μSv/hour, particle flux cm⁻² sr⁻¹ s⁻¹, and available ISS latitude/longitude/altitude. Instrument identifiers are case-sensitive; coordinate fields are currently described for ISS data.
sources.evidence_limitations: RadLab is a curated instrument-level archive; its records are not an individual astronaut dosimeter, clinical threshold, operational EVA limit or direct personal exposure estimate. NASA notes preliminary data and an approximate median cadence in its release history. Missing values and timestamps remain source-specific.

sources.title: OSDR Biological Data API
sources.reuse_status: NASA_PUBLIC_API_METADATA_LINK_ONLY; review dataset-specific terms and design
sources.suggested_citation: NASA Open Science Data Repository. (Dynamic; reviewed 2026-11-15). OSDR Biological Data API. https://visualization.osdr.nasa.gov/biodata/api/
sources.source_scope: Documents REST and tabular query interfaces for GeneLab and ALSDA dataset, assay, sample, metadata and data records.
sources.evidence_limitations: OSDR contains heterogeneous human, animal, model-organism, cell, hardware and processed biological studies. Timestamps and units depend on each study. These archived experimental data are not current individual physiological measurements and are not used by ASTHRAL's clinical engine.

sources.institution: NASA Open Science Data Repository / RadLab
sources.title: RadLab Release History
sources.suggested_citation: NASA Open Science Data Repository. (Dynamic; reviewed 2026-11-15). RadLab Release History. https://visualization.osdr.nasa.gov/radlab/gui/knowledgebase/Release_history
sources.source_scope: Documents dataset-specific status and cadence notes. The release page describes some curated RAD, REM and TEPC observations as preliminary, with a median cadence of 24 hours; other RadLab datasets have different reported cadence.
sources.evidence_limitations: A release-level median cadence is not an individual observation schedule or guaranteed sampling interval. Do not interpolate missing records or use these notes to infer personal exposure, flight risk or clinical status.

sources.institution: NASA Open Science Data Repository / Environmental Data App
sources.title: Environmental Data App
sources.reuse_status: NASA_PORTAL_LINK_ONLY; dataset-specific exports require independent review
sources.suggested_citation: NASA Open Science Data Repository. (Dynamic; reviewed 2026-11-15). Environmental Data App. https://visualization.osdr.nasa.gov/eda/
sources.source_scope: The portal provides mission-by-mission environmental and hardware data tables, including example temperature, relative humidity, CO₂ and radiation data.
sources.evidence_limitations: The surfaced environmental mission examples include rodent research hardware and ground controls. Cabin/hardware temperature is not body temperature; experimental telemetry is not crew health telemetry. No stable public JSON API contract was verified, so ASTHRAL does not fetch or clinically interpret EDA data.
